body:
A pair of top-10 showdowns in Provo and Bloomington lead a loaded Week 7 of action where national contenders and hopeful crashers put their postseason hopes on the line
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 15, 2026

        Last week, multiple losses by AP Top 10 teams shook up the College Football Playoff picture. That momentum is sure to continue into Week 7 as multiple such teams are guaranteed to lose in pivotal spots. BYU and Notre Dame battle in a major nonconference matchup that can nearly write a ticket for the College Football Playoff. Ohio State and Indiana both have the chance to position themselves for Big Ten contention, while Missouri has a prove-it spot to cement itself in the top tier of contenders. Here are seven games that will have major implications on the College Football Playoff picture, including a pair of top-10 matchups. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Notre Dame at No. 8 BYUThe postseason implications are off the charts as two of the biggest religious institutions in the FBS meet in Provo. Notre Dame has only three ranked matchups this year, with the Cougars as the only road opponent. A win essentially locks Notre Dame into a playoff spot after missing last year. 
For BYU -- and the Big 12 -- the implications are even deeper. The Cougars finished No. 11 and 13 in the AP Top 25 in the past two years, but were excluded from the postseason both times. The Big 12 has also failed to produce an at-large since the field moved to 12, the only league to face that issue. Those dynamics can quickly change if BYU pulls the monumental upset. 
        
            
                BYU is playing for a nice resume boost on Saturday, Notre Dame is fighting for its CFP life
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 Ohio State at No. 5 IndianaOhio State vs. Indiana is a heavyweight battle in Bloomington, and the only thing nudging it down the list is that it might not be the only time these two teams play. The Buckeyes have an early loss to Texas, but have otherwise been dominant. Indiana remains undefeated, but needed a late comeback to survive a top-25-caliber Nebraska. The Buckeyes are the only top-15 opponent on the schedule; finishing 11-1 should be enough to reach the postseason, but this is where we learn whether there's championship contention in IU's future. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Alabama at No. 14 TennesseeTennessee sits right on the edge of postseason contention after a 5-1 start, with the only loss coming by three points to then-No. 1 Texas. Now is the time to elevate if they're ready to make a push, though underwhelming offensive performances against Auburn and Arkansas bring up major questions. Instead, this is likely a major prove-it spot for Alabama coming off an emotional loss to Georgia. The Crimson Tide are undefeated coming off losses under Kalen DeBoer, including three wins by multiple scores against SEC opponents. Alabama can reassert itself as a national contender by thrashing Tennessee in Neyland Stadium. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole MissEven though both of these teams are comfortably within the top 13 at this point, this is a de facto College Football Playoff elimination game at The Grove. Ole Miss's resume wins against LSU and Louisville are quickly losing their luster, and the loss to Florida looks even worse after the Gators' two-game collapse. 
Missouri, conversely, has the chance to stun the SEC and firmly enter the playoff picture with a road win. Since a tight road loss to Mississippi State, the Tigers have won two straight by a combined 49 points as running back Jamal Roberts took a major step forward. Missouri's offense is good enough to blitz Ole Miss' defense if they bring their A-game. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 18 Oklahoma State at No. 20 HoustonThere's room for one outsider to crash the Big 12 title race alongside BYU, Utah and Texas Tech. The winner of this game has an excellent chance to take that spot. The Cowboys have recovered masterfully since their Tulsa fumble, winning both Big 12 matchups by at least two touchdowns. Houston's only miscue came against Texas Tech, a road loss on a missed two-point conversion. They need this game to stay alive, as tiebreakers get complicated if they finish with multiple Big 12 losses. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Texas vs. FloridaThis marks a pivotal get-right game for Texas after a stunning loss to Oklahoma last Saturday. The Longhorns have been wildly inconsistent on offense, ranking No. 80 in total offense and No. 105 in yards per play, numbers tanked by playing three elite defenses. If Texas can't move the ball at will against Florida's SEC-worst defense, it's time to set off alarm bells. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    James Madison vs. Georgia StateIt's time to keep a close eye on undefeated James Madison. The Dukes have taken care of business every week under first-year coach Billy Napier and have a surging Georgia State squad on the other sideline. The Panthers are 4-1 after obliterating Old Dominion, and their only blemish came in a competitive matchup vs. UCF. Winning this game clears the way for James Madison to control the Sun Belt race and get into the CFP race.

title: Bills' Bradley Chubb reveals what he said that led to Alaric Jackson punch and suspension - CBS Sports
description: Chubb was trash-talking Jackson after the Bills' Monday night win
body:
Chubb was trash-talking Jackson after the Bills' Monday night win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:55 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Los Angeles Rams tackle Alaric Jackson was suspended by the NFL earlier this week for punching Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb during a postgame altercation following the Bills' overtime win on "Monday Night Football." Jackson was initially suspended for two games, but hearing officer Derrick Brooks reduced the suspension to one game on appeal.Jackson was trading jerseys with Buffalo defensive lineman Deone Walker when Chubb appeared to walk over and say something to Jackson. Jackson was apparently upset by whatever, and he walked straight over to Chubb and started an altercation. The two started yelling at each other before Jackson swung at Chubb.
While Chubb was relatively tight-lipped about the incident when asked about it following the game, he had more to say on Wednesday."I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters, per ESPN. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' "He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."
Chubb played 66 snaps against the Rams and lined up on the right side of the defensive line 49 times, meaning he was matched up with Jackson (the left tackle) for approximately 75% of his snaps on Monday night, per Pro Football Focus. We unfortunately don't have data on how often the Rams provided chips or help to Jackson when matched up with Chubb, but according to Chubb, it was apparently quite a lot. After the punch, Chubb's teammates pulled him back, and he refrained from any retaliation. But he said he's taking it as a learning experience. "Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or have my helmet on," Chubb said. 
Chubb ended the game with two tackles, zero sacks and one pressure. He decided to assign the blame to the Rams devoting him extra attention, rather than a strong performance by Jackson. Jackson, clearly, overreacted to that claim, and now he'll have to sit out a week to learn his lesson.

title: Dodgers on the brink: Facing NLCS sweep vs. Brewers, a baseball dynasty could go out with a whimper - CBS Sports
description: LOS ANGELES -- The quiet blared in the Dodgers clubhouse like a siren. A deafening absence of noise. The kind of desperation that scream
body:
LOS ANGELES -- The quiet blared in the Dodgers clubhouse like a siren. A deafening absence of noise. The kind of desperation that screams through whispers. The quiet lingered over Max Muncy as he sat at his locker, scrolling through his iPhone. Cut-sleeve dark gray shirt with his white Dodgers pants still on, he dodged the disappointment with his thumbs. Instead of getting dressed, he marinated in the 3-0 NLCS deficit against the Brewers a little longer.The quiet muffled the voice of Blake Snell, who spoke so softly that even in the hushed home clubhouse one could barely make out his words. The bill of his black-and-camouflage Los Angeles cap hovered over his face, but it still couldn't hide his disappointment.  The silence taunted Kiké Hernández at his locker, his face pointed toward the floor as he rummaged through his closely cropped, bleached-blond hair, searching for answers.This home clubhouse has known the raucous rage of victory better than any other recently. The two-time defending World Series champs have filled this space and others with champagne and euphoria, three times in the previous six seasons. They made a noise that history could hear. 
But Wednesday night, this place, with its wooden walls and royal blue chairs, sounded more like a mausoleum than a mosh pit. Muted by Milwaukee.The Brewers have simply been better. Smarter. Tougher. Hungrier. The Brewers have a 3-0 lead in the NLCS. One more victory and they'll capture the National League pennant for the first time in team history. They can finish a sweep of the Dodgers, who have been the World Series favorites all year long, on Thursday night."It's a pretty simple answer," Muncy said. "We're playing like shit. They're playing great."
They're close to being consumed by the quiet. A 3-0 hole in this NLCS, following a 6-2 beatdown in Game 3 at Dodger Stadium, feels insurmountable even for a club that's repeatedly proven its resolve. Because across from them, a young, exuberant bunch is not only fearless against the $433 million juggernaut. They can sense the mortality of the legends they're facing. The Dodgers are being forced to wrestle with the end of their dominance. Uncharted territory.In some ways, this is playing out predictably. Dynasties often end with epic thuds. Their demise, when it comes, is sudden -- or so it feels. Their excellence trains the expectations. Especially these Dodgers, who've rallied from the improbable, who've authored moments of magic, whose endless well of talent always produces a hero. So when the dominance dies, or meets a greater great, it feels like it came out of nowhere. So it has been with the Dodgers. Their inevitability morphed into impotence. Their supremacy's screeching to a halt. Withering away is their chance to become the first three-peat champs since the Y2K Yankees. 
The ends of eras don't come with announcements. Or reprieves. And the only antidote for their unraveling is the hope of more magic. Los Angeles heads into Game 4 under a cloud of quiet, searching internally for answers that once came so easily. Once unstoppable, the Dodgers appear to be coming undone."We've done it before," said Hernández, whose personal October magic is running on fumes, "but we've never been in this big of a hole." Even as Snell dealt, yielding just one run on a first-pitch homer by Jackson Chourio to open the game, the angst never left Dodger Stadium. Even when Will Smith delivered a bases-loaded, two-run double off Abner Uribe, one of the Brewers' top arms in arguably baseball's deepest bullpen, the nervous tension never loosened its grip.
This is what the Brewers do. They take the air out of teams, out of their offense and out of their audience. They make it hard for opponents to breathe. Their three Game 3 home runs punctured the lungs of the Los Angeles faithful.The Brewers waited out Snell. They didn't have a choice. Snell, a starter not known for his command, could suddenly pelt a bee in the butt with his four-seamer. His fastball played in the zone, drawing a 46% swing-and-miss rate. He punched out nine batters across six frames.The goal is to coax Snell's stuff up in the zone. But with the slider and changeup working, and the curveball altering batters' eye level, the Brewers struggled to pick their poison.
"Snell was unbelievable," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "Like, he was absolutely on it. Like, this guy was sensational."Yet the seismic shift rocked the Dodgers in the seventh when Andrew Vaughn drew a walk on a curveball that Snell got underneath, leaving it up and out of the zone.Then Jake Bauers battled Snell through an 11-pitch at-bat, forcing the left-handed pitcher to shy away from his fastball. On that 11th pitch, with the count full, Snell had no choice but to go back to it. 
And Bauers clobbered it.His no-doubter traveled 412 feet before landing in the right-field bleachers for a two-run homer. Milwaukee led 3-2. The next batter, Garrett Mitchell, followed with another blast to right. "I just left a fastball over the middle to Bauers," Snell said. "Hats off to him. What an at-bat. I threw him everything I had."That's the reality of the end. At some point, everything the champion has is no longer enough. Whether fatigue or regression or leveled-up competition, the best they can do becomes insufficient.
The Dodgers sent out Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner acquired at the deadline, in Game 1. They lost. They sent out Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2, easily one of the best postseason starters of this generation. They lost. Then, in Game 3, they turned to Snell, another two-time Cy Young Award winner, at home. They lost.
For much of this year, the Dodgers were certain Shohei Ohtani would be OK. That the war of attrition, the force of his stubbornness, would somehow heal the injuries to his right bicep and his left knee. Los Angeles would eventually infuse his once-in-a-lifetime skill set into this series. Yet Ohtani hasn't looked right. He hasn't homered in nearly two months. Last postseason, he hit eight. The wear and tear of his folkloric physique, it seems, has begun to take its toll. His left leg drags, barely lifting off the grass as he walks to the plate. 
He's 32 with a lot of baseball miles on his body. His knee can no longer withstand the torque and power that only he can generate. He has virtually become a singles hitter in these playoffs.And after the game, Ohtani's locker remained vacant. Engulfed by the quiet.Ditto for Mookie Betts. His empty locker surrendered to the quiet. His game turned down a few volumes. Despite putting together quality at-bats in this series, the 34-year-old is no longer the star he used to be.Betts is trying to become the only active player to have four World Series rings. And the Dodgers are trying to become the first NL team to threepeat. But the chance to make history is fading from their grasp. It might already be over. "I don't know the mindset of being down 0-3," Muncy said. I've never been down 0-3. So I can't tell you." Little time. Few words. No answers. In the world of the Dodgers, the quiet is getting louder.

        After back-to-back runs of freshmen winning National Player of the Year, college hoops might transition back to a place where the most valuable player in the sport is someone who's spent three or four years at this level. Duke boasted the best player in college hoops the past two years in Cooper Flagg and Cameron Boozer, but prior to that we saw the likes of Zach Edey, Oscar Tshiebwe, Luka Garza and Obi Toppin make their everlasting marks on the sport.Will another vet take the POY crown in 2026-27? We think so, but our ballots had three players earn votes. One of them was First Team All-American Tyler Tanner, who might wind up with the highest usage rate of any point guard in the country at Vanderbilt this season. Tanner has put on weight and could put up the best season by any Vandy player ever if it all comes together. 
        
            
                2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America Teams: Thomas Haugh, Jeremy Fears Jr., Tyran Stokes among top stars
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Florida senior Thomas Haugh also received votes, and rightly so after he opted to return to the Gators, turning down likely being a top-20 NBA pick in the process. Haugh is surrounded by the best frontcourt in college basketball, which will both benefit him as a player — but also could see his teammates (Alex Condon, Rueben Chinyelu) steal the spotlight from game to game.
Which leaves us with the third player, and our preseason honoree.Shawn Respert, Draymond Green and Denzel Valentine are the only Michigan State Spartans to earn a National Player of the Year award. (Surprisingly, Magic Johnson did not win it; Larry Bird swept all the awards in 1978-79.) After leading the nation in assists, Tom Izzo has his floor general back — and quite possibly the most valuable player in the country. Note: The CBS Sports preseason awards were voted on by college basketball writers at CBS Sports and 247Sports, as well as some broadcasters from CBS/CBS Sports Network.
CBS Sports Preseason Player of the YearJeremy Fears Jr. | PG | Michigan State | 6-2 | R-Jr. Entering the 2025-26 season, Jeremy Fears Jr. had something to prove. The former McDonald's All-American spent most of his first season in 2023-24 recovering from a gunshot wound and much of his second season sharing the spotlight in Michigan State's backcourt. Finally, with Michigan State replacing its top-three scorers from a 30-win team, Spartans coach Tom Izzo needed Fears to take a step toward stardom. He did all that and more a year ago while leading the Spartans in scoring at 15.2 points per game and leading the nation in assists at 9.4 per contest. 
Now, after earning CBS Sports third-team All-American honors while shepherding Michigan State to a 27-8 season and Sweet 16 appearance, he's back for more. The CBS Sports Preseason Player of the Year is already one of college basketball's elite pick-and-roll players, and there's still plenty that he can improve upon. As Fears seeks to make lofty preseason expectations a reality, there is room for growth in his perimeter shooting and interior finishing. After hitting just 32.1% of his 3-pointers on 3.1 attempts per game last season, Fears should expect defenders to go under on screens. If he can more reliably drain triples, it will open up additional driving lanes for one of the sport's top passers. Similarly, if he can elevate his 52.6% shooting percentage at the rim, it will mean that even more dump-off passes are available once he reaches the paint.
The idea of Fears elevating his game even further should strike fear into the Big Ten and the rest of the nation. -- David CobbDating back to the 2011-12 season, here are the players we have picked for CBS Sports Preseason National Player of the Year and, in turn, the eventual NPOY (in parentheses). If we nailed it from start to finish, the pick is in bold. 2011: Jared Sullinger (Anthony Davis)2012: Cody Zeller (Trey Burke)2013: Andrew Wiggins (Doug McDermott)2014: Jahlil Okafor (Frank Kaminsky)2015: Kyle Wiltjer (Denzel Valentine/Buddy Hield)2016: Grayson Allen (Frank Mason III)2017: Jalen Brunson 2018: RJ Barrett (Zion Williamson)2019: Cassius Winston (Obi Toppin)2020: Luka Garza 2021: Drew Timme (Oscar Tshiebwe)2022: Drew Timme (Zach Edey)2023: Zach Edey2024: Mark Sears (Cooper Flagg)2025: Braden Smith (Cameron Boozer)

title: Dave Roberts sparked MLB's only 3-0 playoff comeback, and he'll try to do it again with Dodgers - CBS Sports
description: Roberts, 22 years ago, stole a base that allowed the Red Sox to rally against Mariano Rivera and the Yankees
body:
Roberts, 22 years ago, stole a base that allowed the Red Sox to rally against Mariano Rivera and the Yankees
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:01 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers are one loss away from elimination. The Dodgers again fell to the MLB-best Brewers in Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday night (MIL 6, LA 2), giving Milwaukee a comfortable 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. Los Angeles is trying to become baseball's first threepeat champion since the 1998-2000 Yankees."I think they have more experience.  They're really taking great at-bats.  They're taking better at-bats than they did last year," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said after Game 3 when asked about the difference between this year's Brewers and the Brewers that the Dodgers swept in the NLCS last year. "Their ball-in-play averages, gosh dang, it's got to be .400.  When they put the ball in play, it's a hit.  They're also slugging, which they didn't do last year.  Those are good combos. "Defensively they're everywhere and making plays, and it's hard for us to certainly create, build innings, and score.  Where I thought last year we did a better job of slugging and having those guys play from behind."Historically, teams that have taken a 3-0 lead in a best-of-seven have won 41 of 42 series, with 32 sweeps. The one comeback was, of course, the Red Sox over the Yankees in the 2004 ALCS. New York bludgeoned the Red Sox 19-8 in their Game 3 win, then Boston did not lose again the rest of the postseason en route to its first World Series title since 1918.
If the Dodgers are going to become the second team to mount a 3-0 series comeback, they can look into their own dugout for inspiration. Almost 22 years ago to the day, Roberts stole a key base against Mariano Rivera in the ninth inning of Game 4, then scored the game-tying run. Boston won Game 4 in 12 innings."It's certainly possible.  I've lived it," Roberts said Wednesday when asked about the possibility of coming back from 3-0. "I think the thing is that our guys have been battle-tested, as was that team I was a part of.  I think the mindset has to be -- teams have been down before 0-2, 0-3 -- it's just you've got to win tomorrow.  It's an elimination game.  We've played in a lot of elimination games.  We've just got to get a win.  We've got to find a way to build some momentum, and it takes all of us."Here is Roberts' steal and Boston's ninth-inning comeback in Game 4:
"Even with Mo on the mound, and as bleak as things looked, we felt as if we were still in the game," Roberts told MLB.com in 2020.
For the Dodgers to mount a 3-0 comeback (or even just force a Game 5), they have to hit, first and foremost. Los Angeles has yet to hit a home run in the NLCS, and the team has scored seven runs in the three games. The Dodgers are slugging -- slugging -- .187 as a team. They're 2 for 16 with runners in scoring position. The 16 is the telling number there. They're not even creating opportunities.A comeback will take scoring runs (duh) and likely a signature moment, like Roberts' steal. It doesn't have to be a stolen base. Maybe it's a pitcher escaping a jam with a key strikeout, or a big hit, or a big defensive play. There are lots of ways to have a signature moment in this sport. In 2004, Roberts did it with his legs. Will the Dodgers find a way to do it in Game 4 on Thursday?"I think they've seen the documentary," Roberts said after the Game 3 loss. "They know it can happen."

title: NBA Eastern Conference tiers: Knicks on top, but new-look contenders emerge - CBS Sports
description: The Knicks just won the title, but the loaded East will provide plenty of competition as they look to repeat
body:
The Knicks just won the title, but the loaded East will provide plenty of competition as they look to repeat
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:34 am ET
                        
                •
            
            10 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Eastern Conference has long been viewed as the inferior half of the NBA. Seven of the last 15 championships have been won by the East, but the West has been the deeper of the two conferences with more teams capable of hosting a parade in the end. Getting through the West was trumpeted as a monumental accomplishment. Winning the East was something that some team had to do eventually, but few of them got much credit for it by comparison. That perspective has shifted. The East is stacked. With at least 10 teams having designs on the eight playoff spots, it appears we're headed for one of the most competitive races the conference has produced in quite some time. With the NBA tipping off in less than a week, here are our first Eastern Conference tiers heading into the season. (Odds via FanDuel)Tier 1 -- The Champs
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Knicks (+360 to win East)The Knicks have earned a tier all to themselves after winning their first championship in more than half a century. New York entered the playoffs as the No. 3 seed, then laid waste to the competition. The Hawks somehow took two games off them in the first round. Incredibly, that was the best performance by any of the opposition. The Knicks swept the 76ers and Cavaliers before mounting remarkable comeback after comeback against the Spurs to win the Finals in five games. It was an epic, all-time performance. New York should be feeling pretty good about its title defense despite the history stacked against it (and the attendant pressure of the organization deciding to press pause on contract negotiations). For starters, there are the starters. The Knicks' first five is intact from last season, and we've already seen what Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart can accomplish when they're all healthy and locked in. They're the best starting lineup in the league. 
After that, coach Mike Brown will have more work cut out for himself this season. Backup center Mitchell Robinson left New York for Boston. In his place, the Knicks signed Andre Drummond, a capable enough rotation player but not nearly the rim protector or defensive presence that Robinson provided. Landry Shamet and Jose Alvarado stuck around and were rewarded with new contracts. We'll see how much run is earned by Jordan Clarkson, Miles McBride (whose production and playing time fell off in the postseason) and the rest of the bench. Defending their title won't be easy, but then doing so never is. The Warriors were the last back-to-back champs in 2017 and 2018. Since then, we've had a new winner in each of the last eight seasons. But until someone knocks them off, the Knicks are the title holders. Grabbing the Larry O'Brien Trophy means going through New York. Tier 2 -- The crowded contender field Whoa boy. Did we mention the East is stacked? Each of these teams can make a case for being the biggest challenger to New York's throne, but all of them come complete with questions and concerns when it comes to claiming the crown for themselves. 
We'll take each of these in alphabetical order (rather than the betting odds) to avoid angering one of the fanbases and inviting them to storm the CBS Sports Bastille.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cleveland Cavaliers (+900)The Cavaliers reached their first conference finals without LeBron James last season. It was also the first time Donovan Mitchell advanced that far in his playoff career. Then they got embarrassed by the Knicks -- and embarrassed themselves in the process with coach Kenny Atkinson saying something inadvisable about the whole thing and James Harden somehow going one step further. In addition to keeping their core four together of Mitchell, Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, the Cavs managed to bring breakout wing Peyton Watson to Cleveland in a sign-and-trade with the Nuggets. That starting five is as good as any in the league. The bench is more troublesome following the losses of Dean Wade, Keon Ellis and Dennis Schroder. Atkinson is looking at a lot of Jaylon Tyson and Sam Merrill minutes. And years after the rest of the league sold all of its Mario Hezonja stock, the Cavs suddenly bought some. We'll see what kind of returns they get on that investment, if any.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Boston Celtics (+500)The Celtics had what could charitably be called a volatile offseason. After getting upset by the Sixers in the first round of the playoffs, they dangled Jaylen Brown, a former Finals MVP coming off the best season of his career, in a failed trade attempt for Giannis Antetokounmpo. Then they shipped Brown to Philly, of all places, for Paul George and picks. To say the Boston faithful was not initially thrilled about that is an understatement. PG is seven years Brown's senior and has had injury issues at times, but if he's available, he's at minimum a 3-and-D presence who should slot nicely into the starting lineup. The Celtics addressed their starting center concerns by snagging Robinson from the Knicks, but how many minutes and games they can count on from him is one of Boston's biggest variables. Derrick White remains one of the best defenders in the NBA, but he's coming off the most inefficient shooting season of his career. How Joe Mazzulla, ever the galaxy brain tinkerer, might meddle with the nightly rotation is anyone's guess. The Celtics are still one of the deepest and best-run teams in the NBA, but there are more variables in Boston this season than there have been in years.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Detroit Pistons (+1000) Detroit spent much of last season atop the Eastern Conference standings -- only to barely squeak past the Magic in seven games in the first round and then lose to the Cavs in seven in the second. Cade Cunningham made All-NBA for the second straight season, but the rest of the Pistons were far from consistent when coming to his aid. Jalen Duren made his first All-NBA team, flamed out in the playoffs and then proceeded to get into a nasty and protracted contract negotiation with the front office in the offseason. A five-year deal worth $200 million should help heal the hurt feelings, but how long might any bitterness linger, even with Duren saying all the right things about mending the relationship? Ausar Thompson was a Defensive Player of the Year finalist, but his offensive game was (and might still be) lacking in the extreme. Tobias Harris is gone, replaced by John Collins, who should be an upgrade. Isaiah Stewart was traded to Memphis, leaving Paul Reed as the backup big. Duncan Robinson and newly acquired Isaiah Joe are quality shooters, if not much else. Daniss Jenkins will fill the backup point guard minutes. After Cunningham, the Pistons are once again headed into the season without a reliable second option. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Toronto Raptors (+950)Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto. He's an obvious upgrade in the starting lineup over Brandon Ingram, who was alternately ineffective and unavailable during his time with the Raptors. Leonard is coming off one of his best statistical seasons, and pairing him with Scottie Barnes makes an already good Raptors defense something closer to terrifying. Barnes and Leonard instantly become one of the best two-way combos in the league, and they should give opposing teams fits on a nightly basis. The basketball concern in Toronto is making sure Leonard is around for the postseason. He played 65 games a year ago, but over the last decade, he's cleared that threshold just three times. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia 76ers (+400)And then there are the new-look Sixers. On paper, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid are among the most formidable starting units in the league. The upside here is huge -- as is the potential for the franchise to pull its latest faceplant. How will Maxey, coming off his first All-NBA nod, be utilized with three superstar veterans starting alongside him? For that matter, how will Edgecombe, who had a brilliant rookie season, fit in? How will Brown be deployed with his new team when last season, with his old one, he wasn't asked to defer to anyone? Will Embiid be healthy enough to contribute after missing 150 games over the last three seasons? And what about LeBron? He's arguably the greatest player of all-time, and he decided to go to Philly on a vet minimum to play for a franchise that hasn't gotten out of the second round in more than a quarter century. 
That's a lot of talent, a lot of egos, and even more unknowns about how this thing plays out. Whatever you do, just don't ask whose team this is. Tier 3 -- Wait, what about us?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami Heat (+1100)Heat fans are likely apoplectic about being relegated to Tier 3. (Please direct all concerns to @SamQuinnCBS.) Miami won the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes, but doing so required a bushel of draft capital as well as Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kel'El Ware, all of whom are useful rotation players if not something north of that. The projected starting lineup of Giannis, Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Klay Thompson and Davion Mitchell should be fearsome on defense. The concern here, even with Thompson in town, is spacing and shooting. The Heat could use more playmaking and shot creation, too. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indiana Pacers (+1500)The Pacers made the NBA Finals just two seasons ago and came within one win (and possibly one ruptured Tyrese Haliburton Achilles) of holding a championship parade. After taking a gap year last season, Haliburton is back. Waiting for him is new center Ivica Zubac, acquired at the deadline from the Clippers. Much of the roster that reached the Finals remains in place, as does Rick Carlisle, who is on everyone's short list as one of the best coaches in the NBA. If Haliburton takes time to knock off the rust, it could be slow going for the Pacers. If he looks anything like the version of himself that turned in one of the great individual postseason performances before getting hurt, Indiana will quickly graduate into the contenders tier, much to the chagrin of the rest of that already overloaded category.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta Hawks (+1500)The Hawks! The Hawks were the only team to beat the Knicks more than once during the postseason. Jalen Johnson is a triple-double machine. Nickeil Alexander-Walker went from a quality sixth man in Minnesota to a valuable starter in Atlanta. Dyson Daniels is a defensive dervish and Onyeka Okongwu is an underrated big. Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins have come over from OKC to bolster the rotation. The Hawks should be good. Good enough to break into the contender tier is another matter, though.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orlando Magic (+1600)After years of underachieving, the Magic dumped coach Jamahl Mosley in favor of Sean Sweeney. We'll see if he can make Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner work together. So far, no one has been able to crack that code. Desmond Bane was a useful defender and the Magic's best (only?) reliable shooter from distance last season. As always, Jalen Suggs is entering another season with everyone waiting for him to make the leap or at least make it through the majority of the campaign without missing significant time due to injury. Tier 4 -- Not happening Charlotte Hornets (+3500)Chicago Bulls (+20000)Washington Wizards (+5000)Brooklyn Nets (+75000)Milwaukee Bucks (+50000)It feels rude to include the Hornets -- last year's feel-good, fun-watch team -- in this tier. Charlotte made the right call by moving on from LaMelo Ball. But even with addition by subtraction, getting out of the play-in looks like it will be even harder for the Hornets this season, considering the field in front of them. 
The Bulls should be excited about Caleb Wilson and the new front office led by Bryson Graham. The Bucks and Nets are rebuilding and we can probably forget about them until further notice. As for the Wizards, they've indicated that they want to compete this season by giving Trae Young a fat four-year, $212 million deal that no other team seemed willing to offer or even come close to dangling. They also decided to hold onto Anthony Davis, who has played a grand total of 29 games since the Lakers traded him. The Wizards lucked into the first pick and selected AJ Dybantsa. Alex Sarr had a good season last year. Why Washington isn't investing heavily in its young players instead of choosing this ill-advised two-timeline path is hard to fathom. Maybe because the Wizards can't stop being the Wizards.

description: Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers
body:
Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers

        In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks.The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers. The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500.The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers. The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game.Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks liveDate: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Seahawks have the ballLet's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL, according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide.The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate.
Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles.In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well.Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team (Rams) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.)
The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often.When the Broncos have the ballDenver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2.
Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date.Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere.
The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit.PredictionSean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Pick: Seahawks 24, Broncos 16

title: The Six Pack: Picks for Ohio State, Indiana, Notre Dame-BYU and lock of Week 7 - CBS Sports

body:
Last week I wrote about how there had been a clear divide between ranked and unranked teams, both from an overall winning percentage viewpoint as well as against the spread. It's not the only aspect of the 2026 season that has been an outlier to this point from a gambling perspective.Home-field advantage is realer than ever before. So far this season, in games between FBS opponents, the home team is a remarkable 173-145-5 ATS. That's a 54.4% cover rate. For perspective, assuming the standard (-110) juice, if you'd just blindly bet every home team in FBS games this season, you'd be up 13.5 units this season. That's not a typical result! Going back to the 2014 season, the beginning of the CFP era, that 54.4% win rate is the highest by a wide margin. The next closest season was 2021. It finished at 51.6%. What's a bit more interesting is that this season continues something of a trend.
                                                                    Tom Fornelli
                                                            From 2014 to 2023, that 2021 season was the only time home teams finished above 50% ATS on the season. In 2024, they won 50.9% of the time. In 2025, they followed it up at 51.3%. The 2024 season marked the start of our new superconference era and was the first season when NIL and the transfer portal really kicked in.
That last note is what makes what I'm about to bring up slightly more interesting. In games between G5/6 schools, the home team is covering 57.3% of the time this year. It was 53.4% last season and 53.9% in 2024.Perhaps one of the byproducts of our new NIL era is that, while the richer schools of the Power Four are able to draw in the top talent, often plundering the best players from the Group of Five/Six every portal season, home-field advantage has become far more important among G5/6 schools who are playing on a more even playing field talent-wise.Or it's all just a coincidence. That's the fun thing about all of it. We don't really know anything. Maybe that's why I have such a horrible record in this column so far in 2026. Anyway, while I ponder whether I should start blindly picking every Group of Six home team for the rest of the year if this week goes poorly, you read this week's picks and decide what you want to do with them.
Games of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 Ohio State at No. 5 Indiana: It's quite possibly the biggest game of the weekend, and one of the most difficult for me to figure out. Clearly, to this point, Ohio State has played the more difficult schedule. The Buckeyes have had two difficult road games against Texas and Iowa, with one going far better than the other. That said, Ohio State led Texas for all but the final eight seconds of the game, and as time has passed, I can't help but wonder if Texas won it more than Ohio State blew it.Neither reflects all that well on the Buckeyes, but you have to wonder what they've learned from it.Indiana hasn't faced a ranked opponent yet. You could argue Nebraska should've been ranked last week, and the Cornhuskers gave Indiana fits. They weren't the first to do so this season. Northwestern made things pretty uncomfortable for the Hoosiers earlier this year, too, and it's clear that this Indiana team isn't quite the same ruthless killing machine it was most of last year. But don't let that mislead you. It's still very good and has two gamebreakers at receiver in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh.
And those two could be the difference here. Ohio State has Jeremiah Smith. He's the best receiver in the world right now, but Indiana may be able to slow him down. Not with coverage ability -- I'm not sure any team can cover him -- but with its pass rush. Indiana ranks ninth nationally in pressure rate and 10th in sack rate. If you can pressure Julian Sayin, you can stop Jeremiah Smith, and we saw Indiana put pressure on Sayin in the Big Ten Championship last season.We also saw Ohio State harass the hell out of Fernando Mendoza, but that's the last time the Buckeyes' pass rush looked exceptional. This season Ohio State's defense ranks 95th nationally in pressure rate and 109th in sack rate. That dropoff is the primary reason the unit hasn't been nearly as effective as last season (though it's still good). Josh Hoover has cleaned up the mistakes that dogged him at TCU largely because Indiana has protected him, and he's gotten the ball out quickly. If Ohio State can't suddenly find a pass rush this weekend, I'm not sure things will change much. The Pick: Indiana +3.5 (-110) at Fanduel
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Notre Dame at No. 8 BYU: If you like to follow trends with your gambling, you've got no idea what to do with this game. Over the last three seasons, BYU is 23-9 ATS. That 71.9% cover rate is the best in the country. Well, Notre Dame is 23-11 ATS, and their cover rate of 67.6% ranks fourth. So maybe we're destined for a push if we can find a round number, but right now there's a 10.5-point spread everywhere you look. Good luck picking the right side; I'm avoiding it.
I'd rather look at a different kind of history. BYU fans feel perpetually slighted because their program has been excellent for a while but never gets the national respect they feel it deserves. The primary reason is how BYU performs in its biggest games. Last year the Cougars lost twice, both times to Texas Tech. They were outscored 63-14 in the two games, scoring one touchdown in each. The nation won't view you as an elite team until you beat, or at least compete with, another elite team. This week presents that chance, and while the Cougars may pull it off, I think there's only one path to victory.They basically have to do what Oklahoma did to Texas last week. The Cougars have to turn this into a street fight. Their offense just has not shown up in these types of games. Going back to the 2024 season, BYU's offense has averaged 2.86 points per possession with a 47.2% success rate against unranked opponents. Against ranked teams, those numbers fall to 1.85 points and a 43.6% success rate. A full point per possession is steep.So now they're facing one of the best defenses in the country, and they won't have RB LJ Martin. If Notre Dame is able to take away the run, I'm not confident BYU has a dangerous counterpunch. Yes, Bear Bachmeier has improved as a passer this season statistically, but it's a lot different having success when your arm is when defenses are struggling to stop your run game than when they aren't. We saw that when Texas Tech put the clamps on it twice last season, and I think the Irish do the same here. The Pick: BYU Team Total u17.5 (-130) at Fanduel
Lock of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 Utah at Colorado: It's hard to put any faith in Colorado these days. The team has not performed well on the field, and it's leading to all sorts of distractions off it. Whether it's kicking players off the team following an embarrassing viral clip ahead of a 41-7 loss at Northwestern, or Coach Prime basically throwing his quarterbacks under the bus when asked what the team's problem is. The latest issue has been letting their playbook fall into the hands of Texas Tech before a 29-7 loss to the Red Raiders. Coach Prime downplayed the impact of that on the game, and I tend to agree with him.The other team could tell Colorado what play it was running before each snap, and I'm not sure it'd make much of a difference.This week Isaac Wilson will start for the Buffaloes at QB again, not that I understand why. Julian Lewis hasn't been great, but he's performed better than Wilson has. The decision makes my decision far easier. Give me the Utes, but only in the first half. With Utah having Houston looming next week, I don't want to risk the Utes letting up on the gas in the second half.
Besides, if you haven't noticed, Utah's made a habit of blowing the doors off teams out of the gate. In four games against FBS opponents, the Utes have outscored teams 100-23 in the first half. That's an average lead of 19.25 points at halftime. That's the fourth-best first-half margin in the country, behind only Notre Dame, Ohio State and Miami. I expect the Utes to grab control of this one quickly. The Pick: Utah 1H -9.5 (-108) at DraftKingsUnder of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Washington at Purdue (Friday): Is there a hotter team in the country than the Purdue Boilermakers? Purdue has won two straight Big Ten games after going like a quarter century without winning one. OK, so maybe it wasn't that long, but it had been a while! The biggest reason for the turnaround seems to be that Purdue learned how to play defense.I don't know what, if any, schematic changes the team has made, but the results have been fantastic. In three losses to Wake Forest, UCLA and Indiana, Purdue's defense had a success rate of 47.7% and allowed 4.13 points per possession. In the wins over Illinois and Minnesota, their success rate has skyrocketed to 62.3%, and they've allowed only 1.50 points per possession. Obviously, Indiana and UCLA have had better seasons than either, but Illinois' offense has been good in every game this season except the Purdue game. 
Now the Boilermakers are hosting Washington on a short week. The Huskies' offense has struggled all year and could be without starting QB Demond Williams. It remains to be seen whether that's a bad thing, as Williams has not played well this season, but I don't think a QB change will fix Washington's offense entirely, particularly on a short week when the Huskies have to travel. Since joining the Big Ten, Washington has played seven conference games east of the Rockies. It is 1-6 in those games and averaging only 14 points per game. The Pick: Under 51.5 (-104) at FanduelTeam Total of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Washington State at Oregon State: I remember thinking earlier this season when Houston and Texas Tech had trouble with Oregon State that the Big 12 could be in trouble. This was an Oregon State team that finished 2-10 in 2025, after all.Well, it turns out Oregon State's just a juggernaut. The Beavers have been scoring touchdowns at a crazy rate thanks to the QB/WR combo of Braden Atkinson and Jesse LeGree. Since those opening two losses, the Beavers have averaged 51.7 points per game. They put up so many points on Colorado State that Jim Mora fired his defensive coordinator during the game.
This week, they face a Washington State team that's been decent on defense but horrific on offense. While I expect the Cougars will look to slow this game down, I don't think they're capable of doing so. The Pick: Oregon State Team Total o34.5 (-122) at FanduelUpset of the Week
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Wisconsin at No. 12 UCLA: The following two things can be true: UCLA's win over Oregon last week was massive, and only winning by two points when the other team turns the ball over seven times is a bit concerning. It's even more concerning this week now that the Bruins won't have Nico Iamaleava at QB. I don't know a whole lot about Ty Dieffenbach, but I do know that the Bruins only asked him to throw the ball six times in relief of Nico. Now, there's a chance he won't start this week. It could be Madden Iamaleava.Either way, UCLA's bread and butter is running the ball. That's what they're great at, and it's what they'll try to do again this week. My question is how effective the run game will be without the threat of Nico at QB. Wisconsin has an excellent defense. One that is capable of slowing down the run game and putting pressure on a QB in the passing game. If the Badgers can stymie this offense much the same way Oregon did last week, I think they can come home with a huge road win that sets them up well in the Big Ten. The Pick: Wisconsin (+122) at Fanduel

        This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
 ⚾ Five things to know Thursday Brewers clobbered three homers to take a stranglehold on the NLCS. Jackson Courio blasted a home run on the first pitch of the game, and that was an omen as the Brewers crushed three long balls en route to a 6-2 victory over the Dodgers. Jake Bauers was a hero for Milwaukee as his epic at-bat in the seventh inning ended with a clutch two-run homer. Immediately after Bauers went deep, Garrett Mitchell did the same thing, which had fans wondering why Dave Roberts left Blake Snell in the game for so long.Patriots WR A.J. Brown could return sooner than later. Reinforcements are on the way for Drake Maye and the Patriots offense. The team has opened the practice window for Brown, who has spent four weeks on IR with an ankle injury. That's not the only good injury news this week as Caleb Williams and Lamar Jackson could be back in action Sunday. Still, injuries are affecting every team, but especially your fantasy squad. We're here to help you out with this week's edition of Start 'Em and Sit 'Em.The Astros are looking for a new manager, but the Phillies are opting for stability. On the heels of a disappointing 81-81 season and a very brief postseason appearance, the Astros are making a change at manager. The team will not renew the contract of Joe Espada, which means Houston has hopped aboard the managerial carousel. In the NL, the Phillies are sticking with Don Mattingly, who took over after a terrible start and guided the club to the playoffs.Oregon ruled out Dante Moore against Nebraska, and Florida is now banged up at QB. Even though Moore continues to progress through the concussion protocol, Oregon has ruled him out for Saturday's game against Nebraska. Will Dan Lanning go back to Dylan Raiola after a disastrous start against UCLA or turn to Brock Thomas? Your guess is as good as mine. On the other side of the country, the Gators have injury concerns about Aaron Philo as they get set to visit No. 7 Texas.Our experts have logged their NFL Week 6 picks. The Broncos and Seahawks will kick off Week 6 tonight, but before they tee up the football, our experts have made some game-by-game score predictions. Pete Prisco has the reigning champs picking up a close victory before laying out his picks for the rest of the slate. Meanwhile, Tyler Sullivan forecasts the Panthers pulling off a stunner in his selections. 🏀 Do not miss this: Preseason All-America Team 
                                                                    Mike Meredith / CBS Sports Design
                                                            One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity. That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh. As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft. 
Trotter: "The 6-9 forward passed on a first-round grade from NBA decision-makers to cash in on a lot money to be the face of Florida basketball. Haugh could easily average 17-and-6 again for a loaded Gators squad that is the sturdiest preseason No. 1 outfit we've seen in years. Haugh's energy is a constant. He's an awesome transition scorer who can make hay as a cutter, slasher and real-deal defender. If Haugh can go from 32% to 38% from 3-point range and improve his on-ball potency, he will solidify himself as a lottery pick in a wide-open 2027 NBA Draft."When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part. Big 12: 4SEC: 4ACC: 3Big Ten: 3Big East: 1Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.  🏈 Loyalty is killing CFB coaches 
                                                                    Adam Eargle, CBS Sports
                                                            Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs. 
It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team. Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal. Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it. 
Talty: "Through six games, Reed has the worst passer efficiency rating of any Power Four quarterback. Against the Tigers, Reed finished with an 18.1 QBR (that's bad), 187 yards and two interceptions while completing just 19 of his 39 passes. In Texas A&M's three losses, Reed has thrown only one touchdown compared to five interceptions. You expect more from a veteran player making approximately $3 million this season."Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers. Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings? Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

body:
This year's freshman class doesn't feature the no-doubt talent of last year, but includes a number of intriguing players ready to step into significant roles
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 15, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:54 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Entering the 2025-26 college basketball season, the high school class of 2025 was receiving enormous hype. Led by the likes of Darryn Peterson, AJ Dybantsa and Cameron Boozer, that class didn't just exceed expectations; it went above and beyond. Last year's freshman trio, bolstered by depth that included Caleb Wilson and a cast of star point guards, departed college basketball as one of the greatest collections of first-year talent this sport has ever seen.Naturally, expectations for classes going forward will be high, but fans should pump the brakes entering the 2026-27 season. While this incoming freshman talent certainly is talented, matching the production of last year's class, which included four freshmen on our 2025-26 CBS Sports All-American First Team, will be difficult.The lone freshman to earn first-team honors on the 2026-27 CBS Sports' All-American team is Stokes, who is also our preseason Freshman of the Year.Stokes, who finished as the No. 1-ranked recruit in the 2026 recruiting class by 247Sports and is projected to go No. 1 in the 2027 NBA Draft, is the headliner on Bill Self's Kansas squad.

        
            
                2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America Teams: Thomas Haugh, Jeremy Fears Jr., Tyran Stokes among top stars
                
                    Gary Parrish                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Stokes is joined by Arizona's Caleb Holt, Arkansas' Jordan Smith Jr., Duke's Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje and Missouri's Jason Crowe Jr. on the CBS Sports All-Freshman First-Team.The headliner of CBS Sports All-Freshman Second Team is UCLA forward Nikola Kusturica, who represents the program's best NBA Draft prospect since Lonzo Ball. Also included is Texas' Marcus Spears Jr., who was the top-ranked player in the 2027 recruiting cycle before reclassifying to play college basketball a season early.Note: The 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-Freshman Teams were voted on by college basketball reporters at CBS Sports, 247Sports and analysts and on-air talent from CBS and CBS Sports Network. 
CBS Sports Preseason All-Freshman First-Team
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tyran Stokes | Kansas | G/F | 6-8Preseason Freshman of the Year For the second consecutive year, a player not only lands on our preseason All-American team but is also the CBS Sports' preseason Freshman of the Year. Last season, Darryn Peterson — the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft by the Utah Jazz — earned the honor. This season, it's Stokes, who finished as the top-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports. Part of the reason why Stokes is the favorite to go No. 1 in the 2027 NBA Draft is his blend of power and the ability to get downhill and to the rim, which sets him apart as an offensive player.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jordan Smith Jr. | Arkansas | G | 6-2John Calipari has had his fair share of elite freshman guards throughout his coaching career. Most recently, it was Darius Acuff Jr., who finished as arguably the best first-year guard to play for the Hall of Fame coach and went on to go No. 7 in the 2026 NBA Draft. Smith is up next, as the 6-foot-2 combo guard is a projected top-three pick this summer. Smith's ability to attack the basket is one of his strengths.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje | Duke | F/C | 7-2Duke has had back-to-back national players of the year on the roster, and although it's a long shot that Boumtje Boumtje wins the award this year, he might be the favorite next season. That's because, due to the NBA's draft age requirement, Boumtje Boumtje will have to play two seasons of college basketball. The 17-year-old has a smooth-looking lefty jumper and can impact both ends of the floor.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Caleb Holt | Arizona | G | 6-5Arizona is replacing a star freshman (Brayden Burries) with another at the same position. Holt impacts both ends of the floor and has plus-size at the guard position, making him an intriguing prospect for the 2027 NBA Draft. Holt has a strong chance to be Arizona's highest-drafted player since Deandre Ayton went No. 1 overall in 2018.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jason Crowe Jr. | Missouri | G | 6-3Crowe was the most prolific scorer in high school basketball last season, averaging over 43 points per game. Crowe is Missouri's highest-ranked signee since Michael Porter Jr. The southpaw guard can score at all three levels and should be one of the highest-scoring players in college basketball this season.CBS Sports Preseason All-Freshman Second-Team
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Nikola Kusturica | UCLA | G/F | 6-9Kusturica was a late addition to UCLA's roster this summer, as the 17-year-old Serbian star committed to play for Mick Cronin over Michigan and Kentucky. Due to the NBA's age requirement, Kusturica will have to play two seasons of college basketball before declaring for the draft. The 17-year-old jumbo wing is coming off a dominant run in the FIBA U17 World Cup, highlighted by a 37-point outburst against Team USA in the championship game earlier this summer.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bruce Branch lll | BYU | F | 6-8Branch, the No. 6-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting class by 247Sports, is the latest blue-chip recruit coach Kevin Young has landed since arriving in Provo. One of Branch's strengths in high school was 3-point shooting. He should be able to get plenty of clean looks from beyond the arc in BYU's system this season. Branch is a projected top 10 pick this summer.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Marcus Spears Jr. | Texas | F | 6-9Like Boumtje Boumtje and Kusturica, Spears will have to play at least two seasons of college basketball before declaring for the NBA Draft. title: Rams' Alaric Jackson suspended for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb - CBS Sports
description: Alaric Jackson hit the Bills' pass-rusher with an apparent sucker-punch following Buffalo's wild Monday night win

Alaric Jackson hit the Bills' pass-rusher with an apparent sucker-punch following Buffalo's wild Monday night win

    8:26 am ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Buffalo Bills picked up one of the wildest wins of the season on Monday night with an overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and somehow, things actually got even wilder after the game. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and appeared to make contact with his face.The NFL initially suspended Jackson two games for the incident. However, Jackson appealed the suspension, and it has been reduced to just a one-game ban. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Monday, Oct. 19, which sets him up to miss the Week 6 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals and be eligible to return for the Week 7 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders.Following Buffalo's 37-34 win, several players from both teams stayed on the field to do a jersey exchange, and that's when the drama started. Jackson was trading his jersey with Buffalo's Deone Walker, and while that exchange was going on, Chubb was talking trash to Jackson. The Rams' offensive lineman clearly didn't like what Chubb had to say because he walked straight over to the Bills' pass-rusher and got in his face. Jackson and Chubb then started yelling at each other, and that's when things got ugly.
At that point, the two players had to be separated by their teammates. You can see a video of the incident below. 
"After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the NFL said in a statement.As you can see, Jackson's punch was pretty blatant, and the suspension is unsurprising given the historical precedent for that punishment.
During the 2025 season, Lions safety Brian Branch got hit with a one-game suspension for instigating a post-game fight following a loss to the Chiefs. That altercation actually took place on Oct. 12, 2025, exactly one year before Jackson's punch. Jackson was suspended for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, so this is not his first time standing under the league's watchful eye.Based on the postgame video, it appears that Chubb was talking trash to anyone and everyone. 
After he left the field, Chubb was asked about the altercation. "Just emotions. You know what I mean," Chubb said of what happened, via the California Post. "Emotional game. It was a close game."In the video, you can see that Chubb put his hand in Jackson's face just before Jackson threw the punch and that may have instigated the situation. "They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back, so I just chilled," Chubb said. 
Bradley Chubb put his hand in Alaric Jackson's face before Jackson punched the Bills' defender.  
                                                                    NFL/ESPN
                                                            Chubb was also asked if he was quarreling with anyone specifically and it appears that Jackson wasn't the only Rams player he was talking trash to. "It was just the whole team," Chubb said. Chubb finished the game with just two tackles, but his team won and that's what matters.
